Dark Verse #3

Emperor

RuNyx, Maria Adam (Translator)

4.19
83,911 ratings10,225 reviews
Rate this book
Un regat clădit pe sânge. O supraviețuitoare

Dante Maroni a fost antrenat din ziua în care s-a născut să preia conducerea temutului clan Tenebre. A învățat să-și ascundă cruzimea sub farmec, în costume perfect croite, și să-și tăinuiască iubirea pentru aleasa inimii. Când ițele întunecate îl conduc spre organizația care se află în spatele dispariției multor copii, descoperă un adevăr zguduitor, ce îl obligă să declanșeze un joc mortal.

Amara, fiica menajerei familiei Maroni, l-a iubit pe Dante aproape dintotdeauna. Dar dragostea nu a fost un scut. La cincisprezece ani, a fost răpită, torturată și aproape s-a pierdut pe sine. Ani mai târziu, când aparent și-a găsit liniștea, protejată din umbră fără să știe, un eveniment neașteptat o face să reintre în joc.

Secretele ies la iveală. Rănile se redeschid. Iar dragostea, cândva inocentă, se reaprinde – mai puternică, mai întunecată, mai periculoasă ca oricând.

Regele care nu și-a dorit tronul. Regina care n-a avut de ales.

ÎMPREUNĂ VOR CLĂDI UN IMPERIU AL MORȚII.

About the author

RuNyx

19 books23.5k followers
RuNyx is a New York Times, USA Today and international bestselling author of romance. Her stories range across subgenres from dark contemporary to gothic to historical to fantasy and more, and are currently being translated into over 10 languages.

Her pen name has a very special meaning to her. When she's not writing, she's reading, traveling, meditating, daydreaming, and most of all, procrastinating.

"Amara, you're the beat to my fucking heart."

“You’re not going to walk through life, Amara,” he uttered roughly, each word a vow that cemented itself in her heart. “You’ll dance through it. And I’ll fucking remove anyone who tries to break your rhythm. I promise you.”

RuNyxs range of writing can be seen here. The way she took this book in the same series with the same plot going but from different characters perspectives and made it like it was their own story amazed me because it was so different from the first book the characters and their romance as well. How she handled it and executed it all perfectly was the one thing that she will be praised for by me. She mad me fall in love with Dante and Amara but honestly though she should actually be praised for this book, usually in dark romances you see the same plot being recycled and so much repetitive content (plot and romance wise) and I think no book suffered that in this series.

i’ve come to the conclusion that this is my favorite book in the whole world. whenever i read this book it feels like i can finally breathe again. this book is my air, and it’s my favorite fucking kind of oxygen. i go somewhere completely else when i’m reading this book, and it’s literally my kind of magic. i can’t even begin to explain my love for this book, or dante and amara with words. they have a special place in my heart, if not my whole ass heart. they’re story and journey it’s both heartbreaking and beautiful, and it makes me feel. i will forever be thankful for this book, because the things this book has done to me when i felt like absolute shit is incredible, this book will always pick me up, even if i’m at my lowest. i cannot wait for more people to hopefully fall in love with dante and amara like i did. ngl i was kinda scared to read this book again, because what if i didn’t love it as much as the first and second time. but that wasn’t the case, i actually love it more each time i read it, and i already can’t wait to read this book again. as i said in my review on the first book in this series “the predator” this series is a comfort series to me. but especially this book, because reading about dante and amara felt like coming home. and i can’t explain why i feel as i feel with these two, but i can try.

this book takes us back in time. where we see and get to know little amara and little dante, and we get to know their story right from their first interaction. this book is split up in three parts, and what those three parts are about you’ll have to find out yourself. normally i’d hate that, but it’s written in a way where i actually don’t mind. because it’s not really a time jump from chapter to chapter. we start right from scratch, and then slowly move on from that, along with dante and amara themselves.

side note; as i said in my previous review, please do yourself a favour and go into this series as blind as you can. don’t search it up on social media, because there can be some spoilers ! the first time i read this series, i went in blind, and it was amazing ! because the plots are gonna be plotting. which is why i’m not gonna do a summary, just read the back of the book <3

characters:
amara rossi
my precious bbygirl. amara is such a woman, and she’s the love of my fucking life ! my connection to amara gets stronger each time i reread, she’s such an amazing and strong character. i can see so much of myself in her character, and some parts of her journey. she is one of my favorite fmc’s. amara went through a lot, from a very young age, but exactly what, you’ll have to find out yourself. her character development is so admirable, and i absolutely adore her. amara became the person she needed the most, and that is one of my favorite things in the whole world. atp i don’t know if i want to be her, or want to be with her. her character has a special effect on me, because i can just see her bloom through the pages, and it’s just one of the most beautiful things ever. i just wanna run into her arms and hug the shit out of her, because she’s such a safe place for me.

dante maroni
my man, my man, my man. i’m so in love with dante. now don’t get me wrong, he has some flaws, but he always makes up for them. he is a mobster, but he’s actually a “golden retriever” with a dirty mouth, for his woman. dante’s character is well mannered, doesn’t curse around ladies, as emotionally healthy as mobster can be, acts like an adult, can communicate, can admit to his own mistakes, doesn’t shy away from his feelings, etc. this man is actually perfect. when dante was little, he actually wanted to be a sculptor, and i don’t know why i find that so attractive, but oh well here we are. and as if he wasn’t perfect enough already he also wears reading glasses, as i said; this man is perfect. i think i could talk about dante for hours, and not even stutter. it’s safe to say, that i fell completely in love with his character all over again. and i truly don’t blame little amara for crushing on him, because i’d probably faint if he so much as looked at me. there’s also just something comforting about dante’s character for me, that i can’t explain. the way dante protects the people he loves is the most precious thing ever, he truly deserves the world and more.

“𝙂𝙤𝙙, 𝙝𝙚𝙧 𝙘𝙧𝙪𝙨𝙝 𝙬𝙖𝙨 𝙞𝙣𝙩𝙚𝙣𝙨𝙚, 𝙗𝙪𝙩 𝙝𝙚 𝙬𝙖𝙨𝙣’𝙩 𝙜𝙤𝙞𝙣𝙜 𝙩𝙤 𝙘𝙖𝙡𝙡 𝙝𝙚𝙧 𝙤𝙪𝙩 𝙤𝙣 𝙞𝙩. 𝙃𝙞𝙨 𝙢𝙤𝙩𝙝𝙚𝙧 𝙙𝙞𝙙𝙣’𝙩 𝙧𝙖𝙞𝙨𝙚 𝙝𝙞𝙢 𝙩𝙤 𝙗𝙚 𝙖𝙣 𝙖𝙨𝙨𝙝𝙤𝙡𝙚 𝙩𝙤 𝙬𝙤𝙢𝙖𝙣 𝙖𝙨 𝙡𝙤𝙣𝙜 𝙖𝙨 𝙨𝙝𝙚’𝙙 𝙗𝙚𝙚𝙣 𝙖𝙡𝙞𝙫𝙚.”


⎯ when dante calls amara; “my lady”, “my queen” etc. i always fall just a little harder for him, believe it to not, it’s possible, when you begin to understand the reason why. no matter how many times i read this book i’ll always start to bawl my eyes out reading the scene where dante explains what his back tattoo is, because it’s matched to amara’s scares so it looks like a dragon that’s spewing fire when they stand beside each other. there is just something about this book, that there isn’t in the other books in this series, it just touches my heart. dante and amara was always there for each other, even when they couldn’t physically. dante helped amara through her trauma, in the most beautiful ways. and amara could read dante just by looking into his eyes. these characters are written so perfectly to me, and i completely connect with them, what they feel i feel. these two have the cutest, but also must heartbreaking story. they’ve known each other since they were little, there’s so much more to it than that tho, but read the book ! and they’ve been through so much together, and would honestly do everything and anything for each other. dante and amara literally complements each other so fucking well, like they’re actually perfect for each other. i can’t really go into depth about them, because then i’d have to spoil somethings a little, and i don’t want to do that. dante and amara is my favorite couple of the year along with evajacks. i’ll honestly never get enough of them, and i will be rereading this sometime again soon. dante and amara just makes me believe in love. i hear them in every love song, beautiful or heartbreaking. my heart and soul truly belongs to danteamara.

how i look when i suddenly in my everyday life remember when amara woke up with dante between her legs:


in my opinion an infinity star rating is the only right thing for this book. i love this book and danteamara more than i love life bad comparison since i actually hate life, but you know what i mean. their story just deserves an infinity star rating, no discussions or questions about that. and i’ve actually seen a few mixed reviews on this book, and i’ll shamelessly say, that i don’t agree. everyone has their own opinions tho but like you're wrong.

・❥・ i’d also just like to write a little love letter to runyx for giving me danteamara. the way she has written this book is just so incredible and admirable, the story, journey, characters touch my heart in way i didn’t think was possible. this book is literally my favorite place to be in the entire universe. when i’m holding it in my hands i feel like i’m holding my whole heart in my bare hands. so thank you runyx for giving me this book ! like tristan said; “you need to find something or someone to live for” this book is my something, and danteamara is my someone. when that’s said i will be sending runyx some therapy bills, because i’ve got books to buy so i can’t just use all my money on therapy.

I love those characters and this series so much.

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~



I don’t know where to start. I apologise for the freakin long review in advance, I just had things I needed to say! I just love how this series isn’t “stereotypical” its different in its storyline and the way it deals with certain situations. it’s also pretty clear that the author’s writing really improved here. This one was darker than the previous two, but still so emotional and so raw? Dante and Amara’s relationship was just so sweet? So strong? So real? Those two were just so perfect together.

“You’re the beat to my heart, Amara,”


I love Tristan. I really do, that man doesn’t talk much, but he knows how to make you love him. Now, I was surprised by how much I freakin loved Dante here. I mean I liked him before. But here? He just owned my heart without even trying. Let’s talk a little about how protective considerate loving and caring Dante is....

~ He is a mafia heir who listens to audiobooks in the early mornings while he sculptures.

~ He found a lost damaged boy and did every annoying thing he could do to befriend him. I loved him and Tristan’s bromance so much.

~ He gave her heels??? Amara suffered a traumatic event that made her unable to walk, so he used to carry her out everyday. And when she has healed, her balance was off so she couldn’t wear heels. He brought her heels and hold her hand and made her dance. (No not me getting emotional again)

“You’re not going to walk through life, Amara, You’ll dance through it. And I’ll fucking remove anyone who tries to break your rhythm. I promise you.”


The Emperor is RuNyx’s magnum opus. Amara and Dante’s love is so pure and beautiful, and I am amazed by RuNyx’s ability to create such a mesmerisingly beautiful, incredible, and heartwarming story. The way RuNyx has plotted everything—how she slowly unravels mysteries bit by bit in each book while also keeping us in the dark and on the edge of our seats—is truly a mastermind’s work. RuNyx’s poetic narrative is exquisitely captivating in this book. Her elegant analogies and metaphors breathe life into Dante and Amara’s story, capturing the soulful, aching beauty of their love with a rare grace.

The Emperor tells the forbidden story of Dante and Amara’s love. It focuses on various facets of their lives—from their childhood to their teenage years, to young adulthood, and finally, to the timeline where they are able to shine their love in the light of day. This book is darker and more intense compared to the others. I felt every emotion vividly—from the initial heartbreak and longing of their forbidden love to the deep ache and pain I felt on Amara’s behalf, and the love and joy of witnessing them fall for each other. Their story was as gut-wrenching as it was beautiful. Their journey wasn’t just about love—it was a testament to healing, redemption, and the kind of bond that transforms two souls forever.

“You’re in my blood, beating in my fucking heart. The only way you go is when the heart stops.”


Amara Rossi is the embodiment of a warrior queen. She proved that softness, kindness, and fierce strength can coexist in a woman. She has the purest and most beautiful soul. Amara is my precious girl, and this woman went through hell yet still didn’t lose her true heart, her kindness, or the love she has for the people in her life. She bears the scars of the battles she fought alone, yet she still chooses to emanate light and hope in her world. She never gave up on herself and fought the demons in her mind. I admire Amara’s will to live and survive through hell, and witnessing her resilience in facing her trauma filled me with so much pride. I love how caring and compassionate she is toward the people she loves, especially how deeply she cares for Tristan and Morana. She is a queen, truly.

“He always had a bit of my heart, but I’m not that girl anymore. My heart isn’t the same anymore. This new heart, it doesn’t just love him, Ma. It beats for him.”


Dante Maroni is the man. If you searched for the definition of a man, you’d find Dante Maroni’s name in it. Dante hides his vicious and brutal persona behind his charisma and well-mannered exterior. He is a man who never curses in a woman’s company, acts like a gentleman on the streets and a freak in the sheets, has a great mouth, and knows exactly how to put it to good use. He is perfection in human form. His actions and words always melt my heart. Dante is so different from the usual mafia men in books. They are told that being an unfeeling monster is the only way to survive in their world, but Dante proved that wrong. He never denied his emotions or feelings—he let himself feel every ounce of them, knowing just how powerful they can be. He is a manipulator, and a great one at that, building his own empire behind his father’s back and plotting his demise so he can finally bring his true queen, Amara, home.

“You’re the beat to my heart, Amara.”


Dante and Amara are everything. If I could define soulmates in two words, it would be Dante and Amara. Two people who fell in love with each other over the course of their lives. Every moment of their story is beautiful in its own way—the way they met as teenagers, how Amara was infatuated with him for years, how Dante helped her heal after the tragic event, and how they both fell in love in their quiet moments of healing and stolen moments from their chaotic and dangerous world. Their forbidden love excited me in the previous books, but here, it was heartbreaking. Their love is so true, so raw, and so pure, despite all the darkness in their world. Their profound connection, untamed desire, unforgettable and epic love—interspersed with the layered tension between them—was everything. The angst, the hurt, the longing and passion, the years of yearning and exile, hoping for a better future for themselves—it all hurts so good in this book.

“You’re the queen on the board, Amara. You’re my most powerful piece, but my most vulnerable. They get you, they get me, and the game is over. So, I’ll do whatever I need to make sure they never get you.”


I admire how they work together as king and queen, side by side, building a stronger foundation for their kingdom—it’s the definition of true partnership. I love how they nurture one another, their relationship, their love, their babies, and everything and everyone around them. How much they strengthen each other with their trust and care. How healthy their love is. Their love blossomed at a very slow and steady pace, and it was perfection in every form. I don’t think my words will ever do justice to what Dante and Amara have. Their love is a masterpiece in itself.

“You’re my magnum opus, Amara,” he told her, pressing his forehead against hers, “And I am your humble servant.”
“No,” she whispered, her words falling against his lips. “You are my emperor.”


The shocking revelations in the final chapters? I never saw them coming, and they broke my heart because Amara didn’t deserve it. The epilogue was everything—seeing Amara and Dante happy means the world to me. I can’t wait to see what other shocking bombs RuNyx has in store for me in the next books of this series.

➙ Second read: October 2024 — ♾ stars
➙ First read: January 2023 — 5 stars

i woke up on the wrong side of the bed today (i read this ages ago)

this was so disappointing. i adore the friends to lovers trope. i adore hurt/comfort and the whole “you drew stars around my scars” vibe dante & amara had going on (or so i assumed). i adore stories about soulmates and how they were made for each other but circumstances kept them apart and they fight for their love.

but this wasn’t any of that, at least, not executed well. (there’s gonna be spoilers from here on so beware.)

one of the main things that bugged me in this book was the time jumps and the “years passed. this happened.” narrative this had going on. why am i reading a romance if i’m not seeing the development and progression between the main characters! show me what happened, don’t just tell me!

amara as a kid was such a cutie! shame she didn’t live up to expectations when she was an adult. i’ve heard people call her strong for staying with dante through everything, for enduring all that she did and coming through the other side like a queen — WHERE. she took dante back immediately when he came back to her and she wasn’t satisfied by the ten years of secrecy they endured but didn’t speak up despite dante plying her with false promises.

i did like how respectful dante was of amara’s boundaries from the start because that’s definitely something to appreciate lol and i loved that amara became his person. but i hated how we couldn’t see many scenes of them developing an emotional connection. every time they grew close — cue the author cutting black to the next scene. and on & on. it drove me nuts. why don’t you show me they care for each other more than just the physical/sexual aspect! give me the emotional breakdowns, the fighting and screaming! it really just felt like they were fuck buddies.

after dante broke it off with amara for the first time and yet called her his “queen” and “beat of his fucking heart”, i scoffed and laughed. what sort of love is that, do tell!

FOR TEN. FUCKING. YEARS. they had this weird relationship-not-really-a-relationship where dante appeared in her apartment, they had sex, he vanished and amara just had to grin and bear it. I COULD NEVER. he failed to tell her anything about his life and his secrets and what he’s up to. if he really thinks she’s bold and lovely and the perfect mix of softness and strength for him (as he implies every time they meet) then why doesn’t he fucking trust her enough with his secrets just as he does with his heart (allegedly). it drove me insane.

then of course, dante disappears and is presumed dead by everyone, while amara doesn’t know any detail about it. OBVIOUSLY SHE’S GONNA BE PISSED. the way dante was surprised that she’s mad? like are you stupid or what man. open your fucking eyes. also he said both of them fucked up and i’m like?? where??? yeah she hid the fact that she got assaulted, but it’s her prerogative because it’s her body. whereas him hiding was a decision that impacted their relationship (which impacted him and her!) so he should’ve at least kept her informed. he’s gonna compare something that affects her and is personal to her to something that he did that affected the both of them?? yeah. makes total sense. he has the audacity to say “why did you hide our baby from me” NO SHIT SHERLOCK. you were “dead”. where was she supposed to find you? the audacity to blame her for doing what’s best for her to survive after how she shattered when he left. guy didn’t even apologize at first, he immediately started pointing fingers at amara for playing a part in the destruction of their relationship. how could you just do that to someone for an entirety of ten years and get away with it with the equivalent of a slap on the wrist? it’s baffling to me. amara and dante were about to start a life together. she better fucking know if he disappears and what he’s doing with his life.

tristanmorana will always be beloved to me though <3 precious cuties. i love xander with them.

also why’s everyone related to practically everyone here lmao. dante’s brother is alpha? amara’s dad is the villain mr. x who basically initiated the process of her getting tortured the way she was?

"In that moment, she was just a girl and he was just a boy, and somehow, their broken pieces matched."
I don't know if I have ever fallen in love with characters in a series as much as this one. If Tristan Caine and Morana have my heart than Dante and Amara have my soul. You can't make me choose because I need both to survive.

The last book and this book are simply perfection. I loved this one because we got to see the back stories of the characters. Seeing how Dante and Tristan built a friendship and then how Amara came into the picture. I absolutely adored that about this book. With Tristan and Morana we get "enemies to lovers" but with Dante and Morana we get "forbidden love" and "soulmates". Reading about the two of them and all the struggles and hardships they both went through on each side. Uggghhhh my heart ached for the both of them. I went through three chapters of every emotion I could feel.

I loved getting more of a backstory of Dante and what his character is and even though he is the calmer and collected one out of the two he is also the one with a much dirtier mouth!🤣 This man will fight the world for the ones he loves he just doesn't do in such an "in your face" way as Tristan does, but he is just as protective and vicious.
“You’re not going to walk through life, Amara,” he uttered roughly, each word a vow that cemented itself in her heart. “You’ll dance through it. And I’ll fucking remove anyone who tries to break your rhythm. I promise you.”
Amara is the epitome of strength and perseverance. Everytime my heart broke for her she came back out fighting. She never lost her heart, just like her mom told her. I love her character so much.
"The most generous of hearts, the most steely of spines, Amara was a woman of beauty, a warrior of blood, a queen of scars.
I honestly believe there are not words to describe these books or these two characters. My words can not do it enough justice. You just have to read them and go through all the emotions and fall in love with these characters yourself because I promise you will.

⊹ ♟️ plot summary

the emperor is the third installment in the dark verse series, weaving the intricate story of dante and amara. dante, the heir to the most notorious mafia in the city, finds himself entangled with amara, the daughter of a servant in his household. once a hopeless romantic in her youth, amara never imagined she would develop feelings for dante, who remains oblivious to her affections. to her, he embodies perfection, seen through a lens of idealism. as the narrative unfolds, dante begins to recognize that amara's feelings are genuine and not merely a passing fancy. he starts to view her differently and finds himself drawn to her as well. however, as a mafia prince, he grapples with his father's morally questionable actions, particularly regarding the skin trade, and is determined to make a change. tragedy strikes when amara goes missing, and upon her return, she struggles to reclaim her sense of self. seeking dante's help, they grow closer, deepening their bond. yet, their love faces opposition from dante's father, forcing them into a painful separation.

꒰ 🖇 ⊹  ׁ݂  Where before he had been a man not appreciating the sun until he went blind, now he was a blind man blessed with vision seeing the sunlight in all its glory. Amara wasn't sunlight of clear skies; she was the sun hiding behind dark clouds, muted but powerful enough to still light the dark.

🖇️𖥻 [ scene one ]

➛ watch dante go from this:

"If I'm no consequence to you".

Dante tilted his head to the side, seeing her. Like seeing her. Really seeing her. Uh-oh.

"It's odd you'd say that. My mother used to often tell me," he mused quietly after the moment, his eyes on hers. "People are like chess pieces. Anyone on the board is of consequence."

Amara shook of her little tremor that started at the base of her spine. "And you think I'm on the board?"

"I don't know yet," he said softly, still watching her avidly.

➛ to this:

“You remember what I told you about chess pieces? That I didn’t know what piece you were?"

“Yes.”

He turned his neck to put his eyes on hers. “You’re the queen on the board, Amara. You’re my most powerful piece, but my most vulnerable. They get you, they get me, and the game is over. So, I’ll do whatever I need to make sure they never get you.”

🖇️𖥻 [ scene two ]

"And if I want this?" she asked him softly, hand fingers wrapped around his wrist, feeling his steady pulse under her palm. "What then? What do we do for now?"

"We hide in the shadows for now." Dante gave her that little grin, the one that always sent butterflies fluttering in her belly, and whispered against her lips, "So, will you play with me, my queen?"

"Amara looked into the eyes of the man she loved, saw that same love reflected back at her, and sealed their fates.

"Yes, I will, my king."

🖇️𖥻 [ scene three ]

They became roots of a tree, buried deep underground, out of sight, twined together, entangled together, strengthening each other, weakening each other, taking all the love like nourishment, storing it in secret places, all the while waiting for the tree that had been violently cut to sprout leaves again.

It took time for forests to grow, kingdoms to built, and empires to exist. Where one was being broken, another was being molded to take its place.

They were lovers and friends, strangers and acquaintances, all those things, none of those things.

They just were.
Waiting.
Chip, chip, chip.
Her exile never ended.
They never truly began.

But empires took more time to break people, and it slowly cracked.

🖇️𖥻 [ scene four ]

He cupped her face in his hands, overcome with the riot of emotions she inspired in him.

"You're my magnum opus, Amara," he told her, pressing his forehead against hers, a move that always brought turmoil in him to standstill.

"And I'm your humble servant."

"No," she whispered, her words falling against his lips. "You are my emperor."

well, fuck. this one did it for me guys. i love how all of you know me so well. when i was not overtly impressed with tristan x morana's story, you all told me this would be the one, and you were right. this is the perfect introduction to the dark romance + mafia romance world. this series, has passable prose and easy narrative structure, so in order for the world to distinctive, the characters have to be outstanding. in this case... besties, i fear i love these two more than i love myself.
